plan.rationale: 'Most trusted' means trust received, so the primary measure is weighted in-strength. It sums the 1-10 trust ratings on incoming edges and treats them as strengths, not distances, so no weighted shortest paths are used (use_weights=false). In-degree and PageRank are also computed so the user can see whether the top person stays the same across these definitions.

findings.detail: overlap@k=0.80; measures agree on the leaders

result.explanation: T0 is the most trusted person, receiving a total trust of 1149.0 from 222 people. That is well ahead of T1 (748.0 from 144 people) and T5 (623.0 from 111 people). The main measure is weighted in-strength on the directed trust graph: each person's score is the sum of the 1-10 trust ratings on their incoming edges. The ratings count as strengths, not path lengths, and the full graph of 600 people was used rather than only the largest component. The results are exact, with no approximation. In-degree gives the same top five in the same order (T0, T1, T5, T2, T17), and PageRank also ranks T0 first (0.2047) and T1 second. Lower down, PageRank places T2 and T3 ahead of T5 and drops T17 from its top five. The check found PageRank and in-degree share 80% of their top-5 leaders, so there is no disagreement about who ranks first.
